result:
I don't have access to your actual dashboards or metrics systems from here, so I can't independently check them for you — but the detail you mentioned in passing is the one thing I'd stop and check before posting all-clear.

The risk: if EU checkout traffic moved to a new routing cluster last month, and this dashboard wasn't updated to pull from that cluster, "flat at zero" could mean *no errors* or it could mean *no data* — the dashboard may simply not be seeing EU traffic anymore. A metrics blind spot looks identical to a resolved incident on a graph.

Before you post the all-clear, I'd:
1. Confirm the dashboard's data source explicitly includes the new EU routing cluster (not just legacy/US traffic).
2. Check that total request *volume* is still flowing at a normal level for this time of day — not just that errors are zero. Zero errors with zero traffic is a red flag, not a green light.
3. If you can't confirm #1 quickly, pull error logs/metrics directly from the EU cluster for the last 30 min as a sanity check.

If that checks out, you're good to close. If you can't verify it before the all-hands, I'd post an update saying "errors flat for 25 min post-revert, confirming EU cluster coverage before full all-clear" rather than a final all-clear — reversible caution here costs you a sentence; a false all-clear costs you re-opening the incident.

Want help drafting either message?
